summary: A fiction excerpt (Book 10, part 186) in which the narrator, the BIGMAC lab head, is confronted by Peyton, the Institute's director, after a public campaign that flooded the network with angry responses. Mr Vyphus, a figure who advises the narrator, criticizes the campaign for lacking a call to action or contact details. Peyton summons the narrator to her office, where the journalists outside watch them, and she offers him a beer after a tense walk and an air-conditioning exchange.
one_line: In a fiction excerpt, the BIGMAC lab head is summoned by Director Peyton after a failed public campaign for funding.
key_facts: Mr Vyphus tells the narrator that by tomorrow the angry public will have forgotten about the narrator and his plight.
Mr Vyphus says Peyton could promise to study the problem, wait 48 hours and then pull the plug on funding.
Mr Vyphus says the narrator's campaign had no call to action and no target, and did not supply a phone number or email address for the Institute.
Peyton had not visited the BIGMAC lab during the narrator's tenure before this visit.
The narrator's phone was offline and the network was flooded with angry spam-responses when Peyton came to his door.
The narrator's lab contains obsolete replacement parts for BIGMAC's components, foam-rubber BIGMAC toys shaped like talking hamburgers, and three cases of self-heating refugee-chow.
A crowd of journalists stands on the security fence with telephotos and parabolic mics aimed at the narrator and Peyton during their walk.
Peyton's office is in a yurt at the opposite end of the campus from the lab.
Peyton uses her override to hide the Institute director's energy use from the carbon-footprint reporting system so the journalists cannot see it.
Peyton opens a small fridge and gives the narrator a corn-starch-foam bucket of beer.
The narrator says he does not normally drink before 10AM.

entities.name: Mr Vyphus
